endorsements.quote: Ultimately, the integration of AI into clinical practice should enhance and complement, rather than replace, clinician expertise.

To build trust in an AI-driven approach, regular audits must be conducted to ensure compliance with ethical standards, 39 , 42 accuracy, and quality control, enabling the detection and correction of errors or biases that may emerge over time.
Regulatory frameworks should prioritize the development and implementation of interpretable AI models to ensure safe, explainable, and ethical AI-driven decision-making in clinical practice.
Clinicians should have access to the foundational structure of the AI model and be able to review the features influencing specific recommendations.

unlisted_practices: Establish rigorous standards for data collection, management, and sharing to ensure the integrity of AI-driven approaches.
Rigorously validate AI algorithms, test them for biases, and build them to adapt as new clinical evidence emerges.
Develop dynamic regulatory frameworks that evolve alongside AI technological advancements.
Regularly update, retrain, and revalidate AI models to ensure they remain reliable and accurate.
Use privacy-preserving technologies such as homomorphic encryption to safeguard patient data while enabling cross-institution data sharing.
Invest in technology and infrastructure, including data analytics platforms and secure data storage, to support AI-driven personalized care.
Use a hybrid model in which AI customizes treatment plans under clinician supervision and in alignment with evidence-based medicine guidelines as a safeguard.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/perspective paper examining personalized data-driven practice powered by AI in orthopaedics and discussing implementation challenges, governance, and integration with evidence-based medicine.
